pcie_link_telemetry.method: empirical host<->device bandwidth probe compiled with icx-cl -fsycl, run on native Windows against all 4 B70s (source pcie_bw.cpp in C:\b70-work\bw)
pcie_link_telemetry.interpretation: Sustained ~11.6-12.6 GB/s H2D and ~11.0-11.6 GB/s D2H on all four cards. Real PCIe 4.0 x16 is ~25-28 GB/s and x8 is ~12-14 GB/s, so this is consistent with PCIe 4.0 x8 per card. It is decisively NOT x1 (~0.9-1 GB/s). The earlier 'link width = 1' PnP reading is contradicted by measurement and should be treated as a reporting artifact.
pcie_link_telemetry.caveat: This is bandwidth evidence, not a negotiated-link-state read. Windows exposes no API for the latter. Two-link bifurcation on a x16 slot or a chipset x8 uplink would also produce these numbers; the probe cannot distinguish those from a plain x8 slot.
pcie_link_telemetry.why_it_matters: At ~12 GB/s per card, host-staged weight streaming is the likely bottleneck for this 128.74 GiB pack, so split mode and upload staging matter more than raw compute tuning.

benchmark_findings_2026_10_27.harness: llama-bench.exe in C:\llamacpp-v41\build-sycl\bin, build de5122d (50), 4x Arc Pro B70, -ngl 38 -t 12 -lm none --no-warmup -r 1

results.detail: fatal error in ggml-sycl.cpp:1419 get_row_rounding; exit -1073740791 (0xC0000409 stack buffer overrun / fail-fast)

key_observations: Prefill scales ~11x from b=32 to b=256 (0.55 -> 6.19 t/s), so small batches were throttling prompt processing.
Decode at b=256 collapses to 0.35 t/s, while b=32 with ub 512 reaches 3.69 t/s. Prefill and decode want opposite batch settings.
Layer split beats tensor split for decode 3.65 vs 2.21 t/s (+65%). Tensor split is not the fast path here.
Row split aborts the process on this model; it is unusable as-is.
ub 512 lifted decode from 3.65 to 3.69 t/s and prefill 0.55 to 0.60, a small but consistent gain.
